item.title: Land is as 'saturated' as it's ever been, says Longford IFA
item.description: Longford IFA says local land has never been more saturated at this time of the year in living memory. A rain warning is in place until 11 o'clock tonight in Longford, and the eastern half of the country. The National Directorate for Fire and Emergency Management says the country remains at risk of flooding. item.title: Concern over speed outside local schools
item.description: Serious concern has been raised over the speed at which motorists are travelling outside local schools. It comes as the NTA is being urged to include both Trien and Lisacul in the Safe Routes to School Programme. Parents and staff at the school are said to be seriously concerned over the risk of a crash in the area. item.title: Hopes for greater support for local domestic services
item.description: Cases of domestic abuse will continue to persist as long as the housing crisis remains unresolved. That's according to CEO of Longford Women's Link, Tara Farrell, who says the recent spike in reported cases of domestic abuse 'isn't surprising.' Figures obtained by local Sinn Féin TD Sorca Clarke reveal there's been a 51 per cent increase in the number of cases reported across Longford, Mayo and Roscommon last year. Advertisement Meanwhile, calls made locally have risen by 7.8 per cent since 2020

item.title: Local businesses urged to benefit from St Patrick's Day
item.description: A local councillor is urging Longford businesses to take advantage of St. Patrick's Day and keep their doors open. Fine Gael councillor Peggy Nolan says the council is funding the parade and businesses should avail of the influx of people coming into Longford Town for the event. The town was successfully treated to a new format last year, taking place in the evening to benefit the local night-time economy. item.title: Navigations and Autotests on the menu
item.description: It is set to be a busy weekend of motorsport action with both Cavan and Monaghan motorclubs hosting events. On Saturday evening, Cavan will host Round 7 of the National night navigation championship with the trial also Round 4 of the Squealing Pig Border championship. The Ballymac Inn, Ballymagauran is the headquarters for the event with the first car away at 9pm On Sunday Monaghan motorclub will host their Autotest at Mc Aree Engineering in Ballinode. item.title: Posts remain vacant at e-mental health hub in Castlerea
item.description: The Kerry mental health scandal could be repeated in west Roscommon, according to a local senator. A review found 227 children were at risk of harm in the South Kerry Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service, and 46 suffered significant harm. It emerged yesterday there are several vacant and withdrawn posts in the E-Mental Health Hub in Castlerea. item.title: Government to confirm plans for social media age ban
item.description: Government ministers are planning to put forward new laws to ban under-16s from having social media accounts. There are plans for an age verification tool to be tested to explore how a ban would work. Last December, Australia was the first country to restrict teenagers from social media, while the UK and France are among countries planning similar measures. item.title: Local house prices among lowest in the country
item.description: House prices in west and north Roscommon are some of the lowest in the country. That's according to new figures from the CSO. The Castlerea F45 eircode had the lowest median price in the country at €155,000, with a house in the Boyle F52 postcode €180,000. Advertisement Roscommon's F42 saw a median price of €259,750 in the year to December, while properties in Longford's N39 and N41 Carrick-on-Shannon were at €200,000. The Athlone N37 eircode was once again, the most expensive locally at €320,00

item.title: Longford motorist caught speeding on National Slow Down Day
item.description: A motorist was caught exceeding the speed limit in county Longford. The detection was made in Keenagh. The driver was caught driving 88kph in a 60kph zone on Wednesday. item.title: Man pleads guilty over Garda dog attack in county Longford
item.description: A man has pleaded guilty to permitting his German Shepherd dog to attack a Garda Sergeant more than seven years ago, while his wife has entered a guilty plea to the production of a slash hook in the course of the same dispute. Edward ‘Blondie’ Stokes and his wife Sharon Stokes entered their eleventh hour pleas just before their jury trial was set to begin at Longford Circuit Court this morning, more than seven years after the incident took place.
